docs.title: workflow-core
docs.text:
Declarative, pipeline-based workflow runtime for Python web servers.

Define business flows as state machines in Python. Mount them to FastAPI or Django. Replace tangled service layers with explicit, composable execution.

docs.title: The problem it solves
docs.text:
Traditional web applications scatter execution flow across controllers, serializers, services, ORM hooks, and async jobs. When something breaks, you trace through five layers to find where it happened. When something needs to change, you edit in six places.

workflow-core makes execution explicit. A workflow is a graph of named states. Each state runs a node. Each node returns an outcome. The runtime follows the transitions. The context carries all state.

form → decision → http → persist → response

You can read this. You can trace it. You can change it.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: pip install workflow-core

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
import asyncio
from workflow_core import Workflow, Node, Runtime, Registry
from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode, DecisionNode, PersistNode, ResponseNode

# 1. Register node types
registry = Registry()
registry.register("form")(FormNode)
registry.register("decision")(DecisionNode)
registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)

# 2. Define the workflow
workflow = Workflow(
    id="create_user",
    start="collect",
    nodes={
        "collect": Node(
            type="form",
            params={
                "fields": {
                    "name": {"type": "str", "required": True},
                    "age":  {"type": "int",  "required": True, "min": 0},
                    "role": {"type": "str",  "required": True, "enum": ["admin", "user"]},
                }
            },
            transitions={"success": "respond_ok", "failure": "respond_error"},
        ),
        "respond_ok": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"include": ["validated"], "status": 201},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "respond_error": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"include": ["validated"], "status": 422},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
    },
)

# 3. Execute
async def main():
    runtime = Runtime(workflow, registry)
    context = await runtime.execute(
        "exec_001",
        input_data={"input": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "role": "admin"}},
    )
    print(context.data["response"])
    # {"data": {"validated": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "role": "admin"}}, "status": 201}

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: The core idea
docs.text: Applications are execution systems. A request enters, data flows through transformations, state evolves, a response comes out. workflow-core makes that execution path explicit and declarative instead of hiding it across controllers, services, and ORM hooks.

docs.title: State machine
docs.text:
A Workflow is a state machine. Each Node is a state. Each node declares where execution goes next based on the outcome.

"collect"   ──success──▶  "verify"
            ──failure──▶  "reject"

"verify"    ──approved──▶  "create_account"
            ──rejected──▶  "reject"

"create_account"  ──success──▶  None  (end)

"reject"    ──success──▶  None  (end)

This is the entire execution topology, visible in one place. No hidden branching inside service methods. No conditional logic spread across files.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Each node has a transitions dict: outcome key → next node id (or None to end).

Node(
    type="decision",
    params={"key": "kyc_status", "operator": "eq", "value": "approved"},
    transitions={
        "true":  "create_account",
        "false": "reject",
    },
)

The node returns Result(transition="true") or Result(transition="false"). The runtime follows the matching transition.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Context is the single object that carries all execution state from node to node.

Context(
    execution_id="exec_001",
    workflow_id="onboarding",
    node="verify_kyc",          # current state
    data={"name": "Alice", ...} # accumulated data
)

docs.title: Context is immutable
docs.text:
Nodes never mutate context. They return output data. The runtime merges it in:

# node returns this
Result(output={"kyc_result": {"status": "approved"}})

# runtime produces this
context.merge({"kyc_result": {"status": "approved"}})
# → new Context with data = {**old_data, "kyc_result": {...}}

docs.title: Context is append-only
docs.text: Each node adds to context.data. Earlier keys are never deleted or overwritten by the runtime. By the end of the workflow, context.data is a complete record of everything that happened.

docs.title: Reading context in a node
docs.text:
class MyNode:
    async def run(self, context: Context, params: dict) -> Result | NodeError:
        name = context.data.get("validated", {}).get("name")
        ...

Nodes read from context.data. They never write to it directly.

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
A node is a single unit of work. It receives the current context and its configuration params. It returns a Result or NodeError.

Context + params
    ↓
Node.run()
    ↓
Result(output={...}, transition="success")
  or
NodeError(code="...", message="...", transition="failure")

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
A successful outcome. Carries output data to merge into context, and a transition key.

Result(output={"user_id": 42}, transition="success")

docs.title: NodeError
docs.text:
A failed outcome. Carries a structured error and a transition key (defaults to "failure").

NodeError(code="VALIDATION_ERROR", message="Age is required", details={"age": "required"})

NodeError is not an exception. It is a value. The runtime follows its transition key like any other outcome — a node error can route to an error-handling state, not necessarily terminate the workflow.

docs.title: The execution loop
docs.text:
while context.node is not None:

    node_def = workflow.nodes[context.node]     # get current state definition
    node = registry.resolve(node_def.type)()    # instantiate node class
    result = await node.run(context, params)    # run the node

    next_node = node_def.transitions[result.transition]  # follow the outcome
    context = context.merge(result.output).evolve(node=next_node)

emit WORKFLOW_COMPLETED
return context

The runtime drives sequencing. Nodes never call each other.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The runtime emits an Event at every execution boundary. This is the observability surface.

NODE_STARTED        → before node.run()
NODE_COMPLETED      → after node.run(), carries the transition key
TRANSITION_SELECTED → after transition resolved, carries next node
WORKFLOW_COMPLETED  → after the loop exits
WORKFLOW_FAILED     → if the runtime raises

Subscribe by passing an on_event callback to runtime.execute():

events = []

context = await runtime.execute(
    "exec_001",
    input_data={...},
    on_event=events.append,          # sync callback
)

# or async
async def log_event(event: Event) -> None:
    print(f"{event.type} | node={event.node_id}")

context = await runtime.execute("exec_001", on_event=log_event)

Events are immutable. They carry execution_id, node_id, timestamp, and a data dict with transition details.

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
The Registry decouples node type names (used in workflow definitions) from the classes that implement them.

registry = Registry()

# built-in node
registry.register("form")(FormNode)

# custom node — no args
@registry.register("send_email")
class SendEmailNode:
    async def run(self, context, params): ...

# node needing dependencies — register a factory
repo = RedisRepository(redis_client)
registry.register("persist")(lambda: PersistNode(repo))

The runtime calls registry.resolve("form")() to instantiate the node for each execution. Nodes are stateless — a new instance is created per node execution.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install workflow-core

With Poetry:

poetry add workflow-core

Requirements: Python 3.11+

docs.title: Your first workflow
docs.text: This example collects a user's name and age, validates them, and returns a response.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create a registry and register node types
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Registry
from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode, ResponseNode

registry = Registry()
registry.register("form")(FormNode)
registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)

The registry maps string type names (used in the workflow definition) to the actual node classes that execute them.

docs.title: Step 2 — Define the workflow
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Workflow, Node

workflow = Workflow(
    id="collect_user",
    start="collect",
    nodes={
        "collect": Node(
            type="form",
            params={
                "fields": {
                    "name": {"type": "str", "required": True},
                    "age":  {"type": "int",  "required": True, "min": 0, "max": 150},
                }
            },
            transitions={
                "success": "ok",
                "failure": "error",
            },
        ),
        "ok": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 200, "include": ["validated"]},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "error": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 422},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
    },
)

transitions maps outcome keys to the next node. None means the workflow ends.

docs.title: Step 3 — Execute
docs.text:
import asyncio
from workflow_core import Runtime

async def main():
    runtime = Runtime(workflow, registry)

    # valid input
    context = await runtime.execute(
        execution_id="exec_001",
        input_data={"input": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}},
    )
    print(context.data["response"])
    # {"data": {"validated": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}}, "status": 200}

    # invalid input
    context = await runtime.execute(
        execution_id="exec_002",
        input_data={"input": {"name": "Alice", "age": -5}},
    )
    print(context.data["response"])
    # {"data": {...}, "status": 422}

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: What just happened
docs.text:
input_data arrives
    ↓
"collect" node (FormNode)
    validates name and age
    → success: data is valid → go to "ok"
    → failure: data invalid  → go to "error"
    ↓
"ok" or "error" node (ResponseNode)
    shapes the response
    → success: None → workflow ends
    ↓
context.data["response"] is the result

The runtime followed the state machine. Each node ran, returned an outcome, and the runtime followed the transition to the next state.

docs.title: Example: KYC Verification
docs.text: Collects identity fields, calls an external KYC provider, evaluates the result, and routes to an approved or rejected response.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
collect_identity  ──success──▶  call_kyc_provider
                  ──failure──▶  respond_invalid

call_kyc_provider ──success──▶  check_kyc_status
                  ──failure──▶  respond_provider_error

check_kyc_status  ──true───▶  respond_approved
                  ──false──▶  respond_rejected

respond_*         ──success──▶  None

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
import asyncio
from workflow_core import Workflow, Node, Runtime, Registry
from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode, HTTPNode, DecisionNode, TransformNode, ResponseNode


def build_registry() -> Registry:
    registry = Registry()
    registry.register("form")(FormNode)
    registry.register("http")(HTTPNode)
    registry.register("decision")(DecisionNode)
    registry.register("transform")(TransformNode)
    registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)
    return registry


workflow = Workflow(
    id="kyc_verification",
    start="collect_identity",
    nodes={
        "collect_identity": Node(
            type="form",
            params={
                "fields": {
                    "full_name":    {"type": "str", "required": True},
                    "date_of_birth": {"type": "str", "required": True},
                    "id_number":    {"type": "str", "required": True},
                }
            },
            transitions={
                "success": "call_kyc_provider",
                "failure": "respond_invalid",
            },
        ),

        "call_kyc_provider": Node(
            type="http",
            params={
                "method":       "POST",
                "url":          "https://kyc.example.com/verify",
                "body_key":     "validated",
                "response_key": "kyc_result",
                "headers":      {"X-API-Key": "secret"},
            },
            transitions={
                "success": "check_kyc_status",
                "failure": "respond_provider_error",
            },
        ),

        "check_kyc_status": Node(
            type="decision",
            params={
                "key":      "kyc_result.status",
                "operator": "eq",
                "value":    "approved",
            },
            transitions={
                "true":  "respond_approved",
                "false": "respond_rejected",
            },
        ),

        "respond_approved": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 200, "include": ["validated", "kyc_result"]},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "respond_rejected": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 422, "include": ["kyc_result"]},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "respond_invalid": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 400},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "respond_provider_error": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 502},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
    },
)


async def main():
    from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, patch

    registry = build_registry()
    runtime = Runtime(workflow, registry)

    # mock the KYC provider response
    mock_response = MagicMock()
    mock_response.is_error = False
    mock_response.status_code = 200
    mock_response.json.return_value = {"status": "approved", "score": 95}

    with patch("workflow_core.nodes.http.httpx.AsyncClient") as MockClient:
        mock_client = AsyncMock()
        mock_client.request = AsyncMock(return_value=mock_response)
        MockClient.return_value.__aenter__ = AsyncMock(return_value=mock_client)
        MockClient.return_value.__aexit__ = AsyncMock(return_value=None)

        context = await runtime.execute(
            execution_id="exec_001",
            input_data={
                "input": {
                    "full_name":     "Alice Smith",
                    "date_of_birth": "1990-05-15",
                    "id_number":     "ID123456",
                }
            },
        )

    print(context.data["response"])
    # {
    #   "data": {
    #     "validated":  {"full_name": "Alice Smith", ...},
    #     "kyc_result": {"status": "approved", "score": 95},
    #   },
    #   "status": 200
    # }


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: What happens step by step
docs.text: Step Node Action 1 collect_identity Validates full_name, date_of_birth, id_number 2 call_kyc_provider POSTs validated to KYC API, stores response as kyc_result 3 check_kyc_status Reads kyc_result.status, compares to "approved" 4 respond_approved Returns 200 with validated fields and KYC result

docs.title: Note on dot-path in DecisionNode
docs.text:
DecisionNode reads from context.data using simple key lookup — not dot-path resolution. To check a nested value like kyc_result.status, use TransformNode first to flatten it:

"flatten_kyc": Node(
    type="transform",
    params={"mapping": {"kyc_status": "kyc_result.status"}},
    transitions={"success": "check_kyc_status"},
),

"check_kyc_status": Node(
    type="decision",
    params={"key": "kyc_status", "operator": "eq", "value": "approved"},
    ...
),

docs.title: Example: User Registration
docs.text: Accepts a name, age, and role. Validates input, checks for conflicts, persists the user, and returns a response.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
collect_info  ──success──▶  check_exists
              ──failure──▶  respond_invalid

check_exists  ──true───▶  respond_conflict   (user already exists)
              ──false──▶  save_user

save_user     ──success──▶  respond_created
              ──failure──▶  respond_error

respond_*     ──success──▶  None

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
import asyncio
from workflow_core import Workflow, Node, Runtime, Registry
from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode, DecisionNode, PersistNode, ResponseNode


def build_registry(repo) -> Registry:
    registry = Registry()
    registry.register("form")(FormNode)
    registry.register("decision")(DecisionNode)
    registry.register("persist")(lambda: PersistNode(repo))
    registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)
    return registry


workflow = Workflow(
    id="user_registration",
    start="collect_info",
    nodes={
        "collect_info": Node(
            type="form",
            params={
                "fields": {
                    "name": {"type": "str",  "required": True,  "max_length": 100},
                    "age":  {"type": "int",  "required": True,  "min": 0, "max": 150},
                    "role": {"type": "str",  "required": True,  "enum": ["admin", "user"]},
                }
            },
            transitions={
                "success": "check_exists",
                "failure": "respond_invalid",
            },
        ),

        "check_exists": Node(
            type="decision",
            params={"key": "existing_user", "operator": "exists"},
            transitions={
                "true":  "respond_conflict",
                "false": "save_user",
            },
        ),

        "save_user": Node(
            type="persist",
            params={
                "operation": "write",
                "key": "user:new",
                "data_key": "validated",
            },
            transitions={
                "success": "respond_created",
                "failure": "respond_error",
            },
        ),

        "respond_created": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 201, "include": ["validated"]},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "respond_invalid": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 422},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "respond_conflict": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 409},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "respond_error": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 500},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
    },
)


async def main():
    from unittest.mock import AsyncMock

    # mock repository for the example
    repo = AsyncMock()
    repo.get.return_value = None   # user does not exist
    repo.set = AsyncMock()

    registry = build_registry(repo)
    runtime = Runtime(workflow, registry)

    context = await runtime.execute(
        execution_id="exec_001",
        input_data={
            "input": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "role": "admin"},
        },
    )

    print(context.data["response"])
    # {"data": {"validated": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "role": "admin"}}, "status": 201}


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: What happens step by step
docs.text: Step Node Input Output 1 collect_info context.data["input"] context.data["validated"] 2 check_exists context.data["existing_user"] transition="false" (not found) 3 save_user context.data["validated"] context.data["persisted"] = True 4 respond_created context.data["validated"] context.data["response"]

docs.title: Failure scenarios
docs.text:
Validation fails (e.g. age is -1): - collect_info → NodeError → transition="failure" → respond_invalid → 422

User already exists (e.g. existing_user is in context): - check_exists → transition="true" → respond_conflict → 409

Persist fails (repository error): - save_user → NodeError → transition="failure" → respond_error → 500

docs.title: Custom Nodes
docs.text: Any class with an async def run(self, context, params) method satisfies NodeProtocol and can be registered as a node type.

docs.title: Minimal custom node
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Context
from workflow_core.result import Result, NodeError


class SendEmailNode:
    async def run(self, context: Context, params: dict) -> Result | NodeError:
        recipient = context.data.get("validated", {}).get("email")
        template  = params.get("template", "welcome")

        if not recipient:
            return NodeError(code="MISSING_EMAIL", message="No email in context")

        # your email sending logic here
        await send_email(recipient, template)

        return Result(output={"email_sent": True})

Register it:

from workflow_core import Registry

registry = Registry()

@registry.register("send_email")
class SendEmailNode:
    async def run(self, context, params): ...

Use it in a workflow:

Node(
    type="send_email",
    params={"template": "welcome"},
    transitions={"success": "respond", "failure": "respond"},
)

docs.title: Nodes with dependencies
docs.text:
Nodes that need infrastructure (database clients, HTTP clients, queues) take their dependencies in __init__. Register a factory so the dependency is injected at construction time:

class NotifyNode:
    def __init__(self, slack_client: SlackClient) -> None:
        self._slack = slack_client

    async def run(self, context: Context, params: dict) -> Result | NodeError:
        channel = params.get("channel", "#alerts")
        message = context.data.get("summary", "")
        await self._slack.post(channel, message)
        return Result()


# wire up the dependency
slack = SlackClient(token=os.environ["SLACK_TOKEN"])
registry.register("notify")(lambda: NotifyNode(slack))

docs.title: Rules every node must follow
docs.text:
Must:

  • Be async def run(self, context, params) -> Result | NodeError
  • Return Result or NodeError — never raise unhandled exceptions
  • Be stateless — no mutable instance state that persists between executions
  • Log execution start and completion if running in production

Must not:

  • Call another node directly — the runtime drives sequencing
  • Write to context.data directly — return output in Result.output
  • Import from workflow_core.adapters — nodes are framework-agnostic
  • Block the event loop — all I/O must be awaited

docs.title: Returning errors
docs.text:
Always return NodeError, never raise:

# correct
if not value:
    return NodeError(code="MISSING_VALUE", message="value is required")

# wrong — unhandled exceptions are caught by the runtime but lose context
if not value:
    raise ValueError("value is required")

Custom transition on error:

return NodeError(
    code="PAYMENT_DECLINED",
    message="Card declined",
    details={"reason": "insufficient_funds"},
    transition="declined",   # routes to "declined" state instead of "failure"
)

The workflow must declare this transition:

Node(
    type="charge_card",
    transitions={
        "success":  "confirm_order",
        "declined": "prompt_retry",
        "failure":  "payment_error",
    },
)

docs.title: Reading params and context
docs.text:
async def run(self, context: Context, params: dict) -> Result | NodeError:
    # from params (static config in workflow definition)
    url     = params.get("url")
    timeout = params.get("timeout", 30)

    # from context (accumulated execution data)
    user_id  = context.data.get("validated", {}).get("user_id")
    kyc_data = context.data.get("kyc_result", {})

docs.title: Producing output
docs.text:
Output from Result is merged into context.data by the runtime. Use descriptive keys:

return Result(
    output={
        "payment_result": {
            "transaction_id": "txn_abc123",
            "amount":         99.99,
            "currency":       "USD",
        }
    },
    transition="success",
)

The next node can then read context.data["payment_result"].

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
A Workflow defines the complete state machine — every node, every transition, and the starting point.

from workflow_core import Workflow, Node

workflow = Workflow(
    id="onboarding",        # unique identifier
    start="collect_info",   # first node to execute
    nodes={
        "collect_info": Node(...),
        "verify_kyc":   Node(...),
        "create_account": Node(...),
    },
)

docs.title: Validation at construction
docs.text:
Workflow validates its definition immediately on construction — before any execution.

  • start must exist in nodes
  • Every non-None transition target must exist in nodes
# raises ValueError: start node 'missing' not in nodes
Workflow(id="w", start="missing", nodes={"step": Node(type="form")})

# raises ValueError: node 'a' transition 'success' → unknown node 'nowhere'
Workflow(
    id="w",
    start="a",
    nodes={"a": Node(type="form", transitions={"success": "nowhere"})},
)

docs.title: Node
docs.text:
A Node is a state in the workflow. It has three fields:

Field Type Description type str Matches a registered node class in the Registry params dict Static configuration passed to the node's run() method transitions dict[str, str \| None] Maps outcome keys to next node ids 
Node(
    type="form",
    params={
        "fields": {
            "email": {"type": "str", "required": True},
        }
    },
    transitions={
        "success": "next_step",
        "failure": "handle_error",
    },
)

docs.title: Terminal transitions
docs.text:
A transition value of None ends the workflow at that state:

transitions={"success": None}

docs.title: Multiple outcomes
docs.text:
A node can have as many transition keys as needed. DecisionNode always returns "true" or "false". HTTPNode returns "success" or "failure". Custom nodes return whatever outcome key they declare.

Node(
    type="decision",
    params={"key": "score", "operator": "gte", "value": 700},
    transitions={
        "true":  "approve",
        "false": "manual_review",
    },
)

docs.title: Linear flow
docs.text:
nodes={
    "a": Node(type="form",     transitions={"success": "b", "failure": "error"}),
    "b": Node(type="http",     transitions={"success": "c", "failure": "error"}),
    "c": Node(type="response", transitions={"success": None}),
    "error": Node(type="response", params={"status": 422}, transitions={"success": None}),
}

docs.title: Decision branch
docs.text:
nodes={
    "check_age": Node(
        type="decision",
        params={"key": "age", "operator": "gte", "value": 18},
        transitions={"true": "adult_flow", "false": "minor_flow"},
    ),
    "adult_flow": Node(type="response", params={"status": 200}, transitions={"success": None}),
    "minor_flow": Node(type="response", params={"status": 403}, transitions={"success": None}),
}

docs.text:
Route NodeError failures to a recovery state instead of ending:

nodes={
    "call_api": Node(
        type="http",
        params={"method": "POST", "url": "https://kyc.example.com"},
        transitions={
            "success": "save_result",
            "failure": "flag_for_review",   # NodeError routes here
        },
    ),
    "save_result":      Node(type="persist",  transitions={"success": None}),
    "flag_for_review":  Node(type="response", params={"status": 202}, transitions={"success": None}),
}

docs.title: Input data
docs.text:
Pass input data when calling runtime.execute(). It becomes available in context.data:

context = await runtime.execute(
    execution_id="exec_001",
    input_data={"input": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}},
)

FormNode reads from context.data["input"] by default. Use params.source to change the key:

Node(type="form", params={"source": "body", "fields": {...}})

docs.title: Django REST Framework Integration
docs.text: Use workflow-core for orchestration in Django REST Framework applications. While DRF handles REST conventions (serialization, authentication, permissions), workflow-core handles complex business logic and multi-step processes.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install 'workflow-core[django]' djangorestframework

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
DRF handles: REST concerns (serialization, auth, permissions, status codes)

workflow-core handles: Business logic orchestration (validation chains, state machines, suspend/resume)

# Good separation:
# - DRF ViewSet: HTTP layer, authentication, response formatting
# - workflow-core Runtime: business logic, data flow, persistence

docs.title: Basic ViewSet Integration
docs.text:
Create a ViewSet that executes workflows:

from rest_framework import viewsets, status
from rest_framework.decorators import action
from rest_framework.response import Response
from workflow_core import Runtime, Workflow, Registry

class UserViewSet(viewsets.ViewSet):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.runtime = Runtime(CREATE_USER_WORKFLOW, self.get_registry())

    def create(self, request):
        """POST /users/ - Create user"""
        context = self.runtime.execute(
            f"user-{uuid4()}",
            input_data={"input": request.data},
        )
        response = context.data.get("response", {})
        return Response(
            response.get("data", {}),
            status=response.get("status", 200),
        )

    @staticmethod
    def get_registry():
        registry = Registry()
        registry.register("form")(FormNode)
        registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)
        return registry

urlpatterns = [
    path("api/users/", UserViewSet.as_view({"post": "create"})),
]

docs.title: Suspend/Resume with DRF
docs.text:
For multi-step workflows (e.g., form submission, confirmation, processing):

from workflow_core import InMemoryStore

class SignupViewSet(viewsets.ViewSet):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.store = InMemoryStore()  # Use RedisStore in production
        self.runtime = Runtime(SIGNUP_WORKFLOW, self.get_registry(), store=self.store)

    def list(self, request):
        """GET /signup/ - Start new signup"""
        execution_id = str(uuid4())
        context = self.runtime.execute(execution_id, input_data={})
        # Client stores execution_id for next step
        return Response({
            "execution_id": execution_id,
            "html": context.data.get("html", ""),
        })

    def create(self, request):
        """POST /signup/ - Submit signup form"""
        execution_id = request.data.get("execution_id")
        if not execution_id:
            return Response(
                {"error": "execution_id required"},
                status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
            )

        try:
            context = self.runtime.resume(
                execution_id,
                input_data={"input": request.data},
            )
        except RuntimeError:
            return Response(
                {"error": "Signup session expired"},
                status=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,
            )

        if "response" in context.data:
            # Workflow completed
            return Response(context.data["response"]["data"])
        else:
            # Workflow suspended (re-render form)
            return Response({"html": context.data.get("html", "")})

urlpatterns = [
    path("api/signup/", SignupViewSet.as_view({
        "get": "list",
        "post": "create",
    })),
]

docs.title: Combining Serializers + Workflows
docs.text:
Use DRF serializers for REST concerns, workflows for orchestration:

from rest_framework import serializers
from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode

class UserSerializer(serializers.Serializer):
    """REST serialization for API docs, pagination, etc."""
    name = serializers.CharField(max_length=100)
    email = serializers.EmailField()
    age = serializers.IntegerField(min_value=0)

class UserViewSet(viewsets.ViewSet):
    def create(self, request):
        """POST /users/ - Create user"""
        # Validate request with DRF serializer
        serializer = UserSerializer(data=request.data)
        if not serializer.is_valid():
            return Response(serializer.errors, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)

        # Pass validated data to workflow
        context = self.runtime.execute(
            f"user-{uuid4()}",
            input_data={"input": serializer.validated_data},
        )
        response = context.data.get("response", {})
        return Response(
            response.get("data", {}),
            status=response.get("status", 201),
        )

When to use each:

Task Use Validate request structure DRF Serializer Validate business rules workflow FormNode Multi-step process workflow Nodes Authentication/permissions DRF Permissions Pagination, filtering DRF Pagination Complex orchestration workflow Runtime

docs.title: Authentication & Permissions
docs.text:
Workflows run after DRF's authentication/permission layer:

from rest_framework.permissions import IsAuthenticated

class SecureWorkflowViewSet(viewsets.ViewSet):
    permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]

    def create(self, request):
        """Only authenticated users can start workflows"""
        # request.user is available here
        context = self.runtime.execute(
            f"user-{request.user.id}-{uuid4()}",
            input_data={
                "input": request.data,
                "user_id": request.user.id,  # Pass to workflow
            },
        )
        return Response(...)

Workflows can access user context:

class CheckOwnershipNode:
    async def run(self, context, params):
        user_id = context.data.get("user_id")
        resource_id = context.data.get("resource_id")

        if not user_owns_resource(user_id, resource_id):
            return NodeError(code="FORBIDDEN", message="Not resource owner")

        return Result(transition="allowed")

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Workflows return structured errors:

class CreateResourceViewSet(viewsets.ViewSet):
    def create(self, request):
        context = self.runtime.execute(
            f"resource-{uuid4()}",
            input_data={"input": request.data},
        )

        response = context.data.get("response")
        if not response:
            # Workflow suspended (e.g., needs confirmation)
            return Response(context.data.get("html", ""))

        if response.get("status") >= 400:
            # Workflow returned error
            return Response(
                response.get("data", {}),
                status=response.get("status"),
            )

        # Success
        return Response(response.get("data", {}), status=response.get("status"))

docs.title: Real-World Example: KYC Verification
docs.text:
Multi-step workflow: form → validation → API call → decision → result

Workflow definition:

KYC_WORKFLOW = Workflow(
    id="kyc_verify",
    start="collect",
    nodes={
        "collect": Node(
            type="form",
            params={
                "fields": {
                    "full_name": {"type": "str", "required": True},
                    "ssn": {"type": "str", "required": True, "max_length": 11},
                    "dob": {"type": "str", "required": True},  # ISO date
                }
            },
            transitions={"success": "verify", "failure": "error"},
        ),
        "verify": Node(
            type="http",
            params={
                "method": "POST",
                "url": "https://kyc-api.example.com/verify",
                "body_key": "validated",
                "response_key": "kyc_result",
            },
            transitions={"success": "check_risk", "failure": "error"},
        ),
        "check_risk": Node(
            type="decision",
            params={
                "key": "kyc_result.risk_score",
                "operator": "lt",
                "value": 50,
            },
            transitions={"true": "approved", "false": "manual_review"},
        ),
        "approved": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 200, "include": ["kyc_result"]},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "manual_review": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 202, "include": ["kyc_result"]},  # 202 Accepted
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
        "error": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 400},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
    },
)

DRF ViewSet:

from rest_framework import viewsets, status
from rest_framework.response import Response
from uuid import uuid4

class KYCViewSet(viewsets.ViewSet):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        registry = Registry()
        registry.register("form")(FormNode)
        registry.register("http")(HTTPNode)
        registry.register("decision")(DecisionNode)
        registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)
        self.runtime = Runtime(KYC_WORKFLOW, registry)

    def create(self, request):
        """POST /kyc/ - Start KYC verification"""
        execution_id = f"kyc-{request.user.id}-{uuid4()}"

        context = self.runtime.execute(
            execution_id,
            input_data={"input": request.data},
        )

        response_data = context.data.get("response", {})
        return Response(
            response_data.get("data", {}),
            status=response_data.get("status", 200),
        )

urlpatterns = [
    path("api/kyc/", KYCViewSet.as_view({"post": "create"})),
]

docs.text:
Workflows don't handle pagination. For listing, use DRF's pagination:

from rest_framework.pagination import PageNumberPagination

class ExecutionListViewSet(viewsets.ViewSet):
    pagination_class = PageNumberPagination

    def list(self, request):
        """GET /executions/ - List executions"""

        executions = Execution.objects.filter(user=request.user)

        paginator = self.pagination_class()
        result_page = paginator.paginate_queryset(executions, request)

        return paginator.get_paginated_response([
            {
                "id": ex.execution_id,
                "workflow": ex.workflow_id,
                "status": ex.status,
                "created_at": ex.created_at,
            }
            for ex in result_page
        ])

docs.text:
1. Use production store (Redis):

from workflow_core.adapters.redis_store import RedisStore
import redis.asyncio

redis_client = redis.asyncio.from_url("redis://localhost")
store = RedisStore(redis_client)
runtime = Runtime(WORKFLOW, registry, store=store)

2. Async views (Django 3.1+):

from asgiref.sync import sync_to_async

class AsyncWorkflowViewSet(viewsets.ViewSet):
    async def create(self, request):
        """DRF auto-wraps sync views; make async for await"""
        context = await self.runtime.execute(
            f"exec-{uuid4()}",
            input_data={"input": request.data},
        )
        return Response(...)

3. Logging & monitoring:

class MonitoredViewSet(viewsets.ViewSet):
    def create(self, request):
        execution_id = f"exec-{uuid4()}"

        # Log workflow start
        logger.info(f"Starting workflow {execution_id}", extra={
            "user_id": request.user.id,
            "workflow": "create_user",
        })

        context = self.runtime.execute(execution_id, {...})

            "status": context.data.get("response", {}).get("status"),

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
workflow-core + DRF:

Aspect DRF workflow-core Request parsing ✅ Serializers — Response formatting ✅ Response class — Authentication ✅ Permissions — Business logic — ✅ Nodes Multi-step processes — ✅ Workflows State persistence — ✅ ExecutionStore Complex validation chains — ✅ FormNode + Processors

Use both: DRF for REST conventions, workflow-core for orchestration.

docs.title: NodeError is a value, not an exception
docs.text:
NodeError is a normal return value — not a raised exception. The runtime treats it the same as Result: it reads the transition key and follows it.

# both of these are handled identically by the runtime
return Result(transition="success")
return NodeError(code="VALIDATION_ERROR", message="...", transition="failure")

This means errors route through the state machine like any other outcome.

docs.title: Routing errors to recovery states
docs.text:
Define explicit error states in your workflow:

nodes={
    "verify_kyc": Node(
        type="http",
        params={"method": "POST", "url": "https://kyc.example.com"},
        transitions={
            "success": "create_account",
            "failure": "kyc_failed",        # HTTP error routes here
        },
    ),
    "create_account": Node(
        type="persist",
        transitions={"success": "respond_ok", "failure": "persist_failed"},
    ),
    "respond_ok": Node(
        type="response",
        params={"status": 201},
        transitions={"success": None},
    ),
    "kyc_failed": Node(
        type="response",
        params={"status": 422, "include": []},
        transitions={"success": None},
    ),
    "persist_failed": Node(
        type="response",
        params={"status": 500},
        transitions={"success": None},
    ),
}

Every failure has a named state. No silent swallowing, no mystery 500s.

docs.title: Custom error transitions
docs.text:
A node can return any transition key, not just "failure". Use this to route different error types to different states:

class PaymentNode:
    async def run(self, context, params):
        result = await charge(context.data["card"])

        if result.declined:
            return NodeError(
                code="PAYMENT_DECLINED",
                message="Card declined",
                transition="declined",
            )

        if result.network_error:
            return NodeError(
                code="NETWORK_ERROR",
                message="Payment gateway unreachable",
                transition="retry",
            )

        return Result(output={"transaction_id": result.id})

Workflow definition:

Node(
    type="payment",
    transitions={
        "success":  "confirm",
        "declined": "prompt_new_card",
        "retry":    "retry_payment",
        "failure":  "payment_error",
    },
)

docs.title: Unexpected exceptions
docs.text:
If a node raises an unhandled exception, the runtime wraps it in a NodeError and uses the "failure" transition:

NodeError(code="UNEXPECTED_ERROR", message=str(exc))

This means your workflow must declare a "failure" transition on any node that might raise, or the runtime will raise a RuntimeError about an unknown transition.

Best practice: always handle expected errors explicitly inside the node and return NodeError. Let unhandled exceptions be truly unexpected — they indicate bugs, not business logic.

docs.title: Detecting errors in the final context
docs.text:
After execution, inspect context.data to determine the outcome:

context = await runtime.execute("exec_001", input_data={...})

response = context.data.get("response", {})
status = response.get("status", 200)

if status >= 400:
    # something failed — check what state we ended in
    print(f"Workflow ended at node: {context.node}")

Alternatively, use the on_event callback to track NODE_COMPLETED events and inspect their transition data.

docs.title: Unknown transitions
docs.text:
If a node returns a transition key that is not declared in the node's transitions dict, the runtime raises immediately:

RuntimeError: node 'verify_kyc': unknown transition 'approved'

This is a configuration error — fix the workflow definition to declare the missing transition. The runtime never silently skips an undeclared transition.

docs.title: Events & Observability
docs.text: The runtime emits an Event at every execution boundary. Events are immutable, timestamped, and carry structured data. They are the observability surface of the library.

docs.title: Event types
docs.text: Type When emitted node.started Before node.run() is called node.completed After node.run() returns, carries transition key transition.selected After next node resolved, carries transition and next context.updated Reserved for future use workflow.completed After the execution loop exits workflow.failed If the runtime raises

docs.title: Subscribing to events
docs.text:
Pass an on_event callback to runtime.execute():

from workflow_core import Event

events: list[Event] = []

context = await runtime.execute(
    "exec_001",
    input_data={...},
    on_event=events.append,
)

Async callbacks are also supported:

async def handle_event(event: Event) -> None:
    await log_to_db(event)

context = await runtime.execute("exec_001", on_event=handle_event)

docs.title: Event structure
docs.text:
Event(
    type=EventType.NODE_COMPLETED,
    execution_id="exec_001",
    node_id="verify_kyc",
    timestamp=datetime(2025, 1, 15, 10, 30, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    data={"transition": "success"},
)
Field Type Description type EventType The event category execution_id str Identifies the execution run node_id str \| None The node that emitted the event timestamp datetime UTC timestamp, set automatically data dict Event-specific payload

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger("workflow")

def log_event(event: Event) -> None:
    logger.info(
        "%s node=%s execution=%s",
        event.type.value,
        event.node_id,
        event.execution_id,
        extra=event.data,
    )

context = await runtime.execute("exec_001", on_event=log_event)

docs.title: Measuring execution time
docs.text:
from datetime import datetime, timezone

start_times: dict[str, datetime] = {}

def track_timing(event: Event) -> None:
    if event.type == EventType.NODE_STARTED and event.node_id:
        start_times[event.node_id] = event.timestamp

    if event.type == EventType.NODE_COMPLETED and event.node_id:
        started = start_times.get(event.node_id)
        if started:
            duration_ms = (event.timestamp - started).total_seconds() * 1000
            print(f"{event.node_id} took {duration_ms:.1f}ms")

docs.title: Audit trail
docs.text:
audit_log: list[dict] = []

def audit(event: Event) -> None:
    if event.type in (EventType.NODE_COMPLETED, EventType.WORKFLOW_COMPLETED):
        audit_log.append({
            "execution_id": event.execution_id,
            "event":        event.type.value,
            "node":         event.node_id,
            "timestamp":    event.timestamp.isoformat(),
            "data":         event.data,
        })

docs.title: SSE streaming (FastAPI)
docs.text:
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
import json

async def execute_and_stream(execution_id: str, input_data: dict):
    async def event_stream():
        async def push(event: Event) -> None:
            payload = json.dumps({
                "type": event.type.value,
                "node": event.node_id,
                "data": event.data,
            })
            yield f"data: {payload}\n\n"

        context = await runtime.execute(execution_id, input_data, on_event=push)
        yield f"data: {json.dumps({'done': True})}\n\n"

    return StreamingResponse(event_stream(), media_type="text/event-stream")

docs.title: Replayability
docs.text:
Because events are immutable and timestamped, you can store them and replay execution history:

# store all events
stored_events: list[dict] = []

async def persist_event(event: Event) -> None:
    stored_events.append(event.model_dump())

await runtime.execute("exec_001", input_data={...}, on_event=persist_event)

# later: reconstruct what happened
for event in stored_events:
    print(f"[{event['timestamp']}] {event['type']} @ {event['node_id']}")

docs.title: FastAPI Integration
docs.text: Mount workflows to a FastAPI application with two routers: api_router for JSON APIs and ui_router for HTML forms.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install 'workflow-core[fastapi]'

docs.title: API Router
docs.text:
Expose workflows as JSON endpoints.

from fastapi import FastAPI
from workflow_core import Runtime, Workflow, Node, Registry
from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode, ResponseNode
from workflow_core.adapters.fastapi import api_router

workflow = Workflow(
    id="create_user",
    start="validate",
    nodes={
        "validate": Node(
            type="form",
            params={"fields": {"name": {"type": "str"}}},
            transitions={"success": "respond", "failure": "respond"},
        ),
        "respond": Node(type="response", transitions={"success": None}),
    },
)

registry = Registry()
registry.register("form")(FormNode)
registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)

runtime = Runtime(workflow, registry)

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(api_router(runtime))

Routes:

Method Path Behavior POST /execute Auto-generate execution_id POST /execute/{execution_id} Use specific execution_id

Both accept JSON body and return JSON response with the workflow result.

# Start execution with auto-generated ID
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/execute \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Alice"}'

# Start with specific execution ID
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/execute/user-123 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Bob"}'

docs.title: UI Router
docs.text:
Mount workflows as server-side-rendered forms with HTMX support.

from workflow_core import InMemoryStore
from workflow_core.adapters.fastapi import ui_router

store = InMemoryStore()
runtime = Runtime(workflow, registry, store=store)

app.include_router(ui_router(runtime, prefix="/forms"))

Routes:

Method Path Behavior GET /forms/new Start fresh execution, render first form GET /{execution_id} Resume execution, render current step POST /{execution_id} Submit form data, advance workflow

docs.title: Form Flow
docs.text:
1. GET /forms/new — Create new execution, render initial form
  2. POST /{execution_id} — Submit form data
  3. If validation fails → re-render with errors
  4. If validation passes → advance to next node
  5. GET /{execution_id} — Resume suspended execution (after POST, before next interaction)

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Use Jinja2 templates with the UINode:

import jinja2

env = jinja2.Environment(loader=jinja2.FileSystemLoader("templates"))

workflow = Workflow(
    id="signup",
    start="collect",
    nodes={
        "collect": Node(
            type="ui",
            params={
                "template": "form.html",
                "partial_template": "_form.html",  # For HTMX
                "fields": {
                    "email": {"type": "str", "required": True},
                    "age": {"type": "int", "required": True, "min": 18},
                },
            },
            transitions={"render": None, "submitted": "confirm", "error": None},
        ),
        "confirm": Node(type="response", transitions={"success": None}),
    },
)

registry.register("ui")(lambda: UINode(env))

Variable Type Description data dict Current execution context data fields dict Field schema from node params errors dict Validation errors (key → message) execution_id str Current execution ID node str Current node ID
