docs.title: Form Data Types
docs.text:
HTML forms submit all data as strings. The adapter automatically coerces values to expected types:

Schema Type Input String Coerced Value "int" "30" 30 "float" "3.14" 3.14 "bool" "true" True "str" "hello" "hello"

Invalid coercions fail validation (e.g., "abc" → int fails type check).

docs.title: Execution Persistence
docs.text:
Both routers support persistence for suspend/resume workflows:

from workflow_core import InMemoryStore

store = InMemoryStore()  # Development only
runtime = Runtime(workflow, registry, store=store)

For production, use Redis:

# (not yet implemented)
# from workflow_core.adapters.redis import RedisStore
# store = RedisStore(redis_client)

The runtime suspends on transitions in the default suspend_on set: {"render", "error"}. Suspended executions are saved to the store and can be resumed later.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Missing execution ID returns 404:

{
  "error": "Execution 'unknown-id' not found",
  "status_code": 404
}

Validation errors render the form with error messages:

<!-- re-rendered with errors dict populated -->
<p class="error">age: must be >= 18</p>

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
import jinja2
from workflow_core import (
    Workflow, Node, Registry, Runtime, InMemoryStore,
)
from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode, ResponseNode
from workflow_core.nodes.ui import UINode
from workflow_core.adapters.fastapi import api_router, ui_router

# Define workflow
workflow = Workflow(
    id="signup",
    start="form",
    nodes={
        "form": Node(
            type="ui",
            params={
                "template": "form.html",
                "fields": {
                    "name": {"type": "str", "required": True},
                    "age": {"type": "int", "required": True, "min": 18},
                },
            },
            transitions={"render": None, "submitted": "done", "error": None},
        ),
        "done": Node(
            type="response",
            params={"status": 200},
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
    },
)

# Register nodes
registry = Registry()
env = jinja2.Environment(loader=jinja2.FileSystemLoader("templates"))
registry.register("ui")(lambda: UINode(env))
registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)

# Create runtime and app
store = InMemoryStore()
runtime = Runtime(workflow, registry, store=store)

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(api_router(runtime, prefix="/api"))
app.include_router(ui_router(runtime, prefix="/ui"))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)

Then visit http://localhost:8000/ui/new to start a workflow.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Context

Carries all execution state through the workflow. Immutable — every modification produces a new instance.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description execution_id str Identifies the execution run workflow_id str ID of the workflow being executed node str \| None Current node ID. None when the workflow has ended data dict[str, Any] Accumulated execution data

docs.title: evolve(**changes) → Context
docs.text:
Produces a new Context with the given fields changed. All other fields are preserved.

next_context = context.evolve(node="next_step")

Used by the runtime to advance to the next node.

docs.title: merge(output: dict) → Context
docs.text:
Produces a new Context with output merged into data. Existing keys in data are overwritten by keys in output.

updated = context.merge({"user_id": 42, "email": "a@b.com"})

Used by the runtime after each node completes to incorporate node output.

docs.title: Immutability
docs.text:
Context is a frozen Pydantic model. Direct attribute assignment raises ValidationError:

context.node = "next"  # raises ValidationError

Always use evolve() or merge():

context = context.evolve(node="next")
context = context.merge({"result": value})

docs.title: Data is append-only by convention
docs.text: The runtime merges node output using merge(), which can overwrite earlier keys if a later node produces the same key. By convention, nodes should use distinct output keys to preserve the full execution record in context.data.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# initial context (created by Runtime)
context = Context(
    execution_id="exec_001",
    workflow_id="onboarding",
    node="collect_info",
    data={"input": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}},
)

# after FormNode runs:
context = context.merge({"validated": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}}).evolve(node="verify_kyc")

# after HTTPNode runs:
context = context.merge({"kyc_result": {"status": "approved"}}).evolve(node="create_account")

# final context (node is None → workflow ended)
context.data
# {
#   "input":       {"name": "Alice", "age": 30},
#   "validated":   {"name": "Alice", "age": 30},
#   "kyc_result":  {"status": "approved"},
#   "response":    {"data": {...}, "status": 201},
# }

docs.title: Event
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Event, EventType

Emitted by the runtime at every execution boundary. Immutable and timestamped.

docs.title: Event fields
docs.text: Field Type Description type EventType Event category execution_id str Identifies the execution run node_id str \| None The node that emitted the event. None for workflow-level events timestamp datetime UTC timestamp, set automatically data dict[str, Any] Event payload

docs.title: EventType
docs.text: Value Constant data keys "node.started" EventType.NODE_STARTED — "node.completed" EventType.NODE_COMPLETED transition "transition.selected" EventType.TRANSITION_SELECTED transition, next "context.updated" EventType.CONTEXT_UPDATED reserved "workflow.completed" EventType.WORKFLOW_COMPLETED — "workflow.failed" EventType.WORKFLOW_FAILED —

docs.title: Subscribing
docs.text:
Pass on_event to runtime.execute(). Both sync and async callbacks are supported:

# sync
context = await runtime.execute("e1", on_event=print)

# async
async def on_event(event: Event) -> None:
    await save_to_audit_log(event)

context = await runtime.execute("e1", on_event=on_event)

See Events & Observability for patterns.

docs.title: Processors
docs.text: Processors are pure async functions that transform execution context. They are the building blocks for composing custom nodes.

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
Processor = Callable[[Context], Awaitable[Context | NodeError]]

A processor receives a context, performs validation or transformation, and returns either an updated context or an error.

docs.title: pipe
docs.text:
Compose processors left-to-right with short-circuit on error.

from workflow_core import pipe, validate_fields, call_http

pipeline = pipe(
    validate_fields({"email": {"type": "str"}}),
    call_http("POST", "https://api.example.com/verify", body_key="validated"),
)

result = await pipeline(context)

If any processor returns NodeError, the pipeline stops and returns that error. Otherwise, context flows through each processor in sequence.

docs.title: validate_fields
docs.text:
Validate and coerce form input fields.

validate_fields(
    fields: dict[str, dict],
    source: str = "input",
) -> Processor

Parameters:

  • fields: Schema defining field rules (type, required, min/max, enum, length)
  • source: Key in context.data to read input from (default: "input")

Field Rules:

{
    "age": {
        "type": "int",           # str, int, float, bool
        "required": True,        # (default True)
        "min": 0,                # numeric only
        "max": 150,              # numeric only
        "min_length": 3,         # string only
        "max_length": 100,       # string only
        "enum": ["admin", "user"],  # whitelist values
    }
}

Behavior:

  • Coerces string values to expected type (e.g., form "30" → int 30)
  • Returns NodeError("VALIDATION_ERROR") with per-field error messages if validation fails
  • Merges {"validated": {...}} on success

Example:

result = await validate_fields({
    "name": {"type": "str", "required": True},
    "age": {"type": "int", "min": 18},
})(context)

if isinstance(result, NodeError):
    return result  # validation failed

# result.data["validated"] = {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}

docs.title: check_condition
docs.text:
Evaluate a single condition against context data.

check_condition(
    key: str,
    operator: str = "eq",
    value: Any = None,
) -> Processor

Operators:

Operator Behavior eq Equal neq Not equal gt Greater than gte Greater than or equal lt Less than lte Less than or equal in In list not_in Not in list exists Value is not None not_exists Value is None

Behavior:

Merges {"_matched": bool} into context. Used by DecisionNode to choose transitions.

Example:

result = await check_condition("status", "eq", "approved")(context)
# result.data["_matched"] = True or False

docs.title: call_http
docs.text:
Make an async HTTP request and merge response into context.

call_http(
    method: str,
    url: str,
    body_key: str | None = None,
    response_key: str = "http_response",
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> Processor

Behavior:

  • Reads request body from context.data[body_key] (if specified)
  • Makes HTTP request, parses JSON response
  • Merges {response_key: response_json} on success
  • Returns NodeError on HTTP error (4xx/5xx) or connection error

Example:

result = await call_http(
    method="POST",
    url="https://api.example.com/users",
    body_key="validated",
    response_key="user",
)(context)

if isinstance(result, NodeError):
    return result

# result.data["user"] = {...response JSON...}

docs.title: map_fields
docs.text:
Map fields using dot-path notation.

map_fields(mapping: dict[str, str]) -> Processor

Parameters:

mapping: Dict of {target: "source.path"}. Uses dot notation to traverse nested objects.

Behavior:

  • Reads values from context.data using source paths
  • Merges mapped values into context
  • Missing paths are silently excluded (no error)

Example:

result = await map_fields({
    "user_id": "kyc.user_id",
    "risk_score": "kyc.result.risk_score",
})(context)

if "kyc.result.risk_score" exists in context, merges it as "risk_score"

docs.title: write_record
docs.text:
Write context data to a repository.

write_record(
    repo: Repository,
    key: str,
    data_key: str = "validated",
) -> Processor

Behavior:

  • Reads data from context.data[data_key]
  • Calls await repo.set(key, data)
  • Merges {"persisted": True} on success

docs.title: read_record
docs.text:
Read data from a repository.

read_record(
    repo: Repository,
    key: str,
    output_key: str = "record",
) -> Processor

Behavior:

  • Calls await repo.get(key)
  • Returns NodeError("NOT_FOUND") if record not found
  • Merges {output_key: record_data} on success

docs.title: delete_record
docs.text:
Delete a record from a repository.

delete_record(repo: Repository, key: str) -> Processor

Behavior:

  • Calls await repo.delete(key)
  • Merges {"deleted": True} on success

docs.title: shape_response
docs.text:
Shape the final HTTP response.

shape_response(
    include: list[str] | None = None,
    status: int = 200,
) -> Processor

Behavior:

  • Filters context.data to only keys in include (if specified)
  • Merges {"response": {"data": {...}, "status": <code>}}

Example:

result = await shape_response(include=["user_id"], status=201)(context)

# result.data["response"] = {
#     "data": {"user_id": 123},
#     "status": 201
# }

docs.title: render_template
docs.text:
Render a Jinja2 template and merge HTML into context.

render_template(
    env: jinja2.Environment,
    template: str,
    partial: str | None = None,
    fields: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    errors: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> Processor

Behavior:

  • If HTMX request and partial provided, renders partial
  • Otherwise renders template
  • Passes variables: data, fields, errors, execution_id, node
  • Merges {"html": rendered_html} on success
  • Returns NodeError("TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND") if template missing

Example:

env = jinja2.Environment(loader=jinja2.FileSystemLoader("templates"))

result = await render_template(
    env,
    template="form.html",
    partial="_form.html",
    fields={"name": {}, "age": {}},
)(context)

# result.data["html"] = "...rendered HTML..."

docs.title: Composing Custom Processors
docs.text:
Create custom processors by implementing the Processor type:

async def my_processor(context: Context) -> Context | NodeError:
    # Do something with context
    if error_condition:
        return NodeError(code="MY_ERROR", message="...")

    # Return modified context
    return context.merge({"my_key": "my_value"})

Then compose with pipe:

result = await pipe(
    validate_fields(fields),
    my_processor,
    call_http("POST", url),
)(context)

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All processors either return a modified Context or a NodeError. The pipe combinator short-circuits on NodeError:

result = await pipe(
    validate_fields(fields),  # fails, returns NodeError
    call_http(...),           # never runs
)(context)

assert isinstance(result, NodeError)
assert result.code == "VALIDATION_ERROR"

Nodes check the result type and decide how to handle errors:

result = await my_processor(context)
if isinstance(result, NodeError):
    return result  # Return error to runtime

docs.title: NodeProtocol
docs.text:
from workflow_core import NodeProtocol

The interface every node must satisfy. Uses structural typing (typing.Protocol) — no inheritance required.

docs.title: Protocol definition
docs.text:
class NodeProtocol(Protocol):
    async def run(self, context: Context, params: dict[str, Any]) -> Result | NodeError:
        ...

Any class with this method signature satisfies the protocol.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Param Type Description context Context Current immutable execution state. Read from context.data. Never write to it. params dict[str, Any] Static configuration from Node.params in the workflow definition

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
Type When Result Node completed successfully NodeError Node encountered a handled failure

Never raise exceptions — always return NodeError.

docs.title: Minimal implementation
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Context
from workflow_core.result import Result, NodeError


class MyNode:
    async def run(self, context: Context, params: dict) -> Result | NodeError:
        value = context.data.get("some_key")

        if not value:
            return NodeError(code="MISSING_VALUE", message="some_key not in context")

        return Result(output={"processed": value})

See Custom Nodes for full guidance.

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Registry

Maps node type strings to node classes (or factories). The runtime uses it to resolve and instantiate nodes during execution.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
registry = Registry()

Each Registry instance maintains its own isolated mapping. Create one per application.

docs.title: register()
docs.text:
def register(type_name: str) -> Callable[[type], type]

Decorator that registers a node class under a type name.

@registry.register("form")
class FormNode:
    async def run(self, context, params): ...

Can also be used as a regular call:

registry.register("form")(FormNode)

Raises ValueError if type_name is already registered.

docs.title: Registering factories
docs.text:
Any callable that returns a node instance can be registered. Use this to inject dependencies:

# inject a Redis repository into PersistNode
repo = RedisRepository(redis_client)
registry.register("persist")(lambda: PersistNode(repo))

# inject an HTTP client into a custom node
http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0)
registry.register("notify")(lambda: NotifyNode(http_client))

docs.title: resolve()
docs.text:
def resolve(type_name: str) -> type

Returns the registered callable for a type name. Raises KeyError if not registered.

The runtime calls registry.resolve(node_def.type)() to instantiate the node for each execution.

docs.title: in operator
docs.text:
"form" in registry    # True if registered
"missing" in registry # False

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Registry
from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode, DecisionNode, HTTPNode, ResponseNode
from workflow_core.nodes import PersistNode

# built-in nodes
registry = Registry()
registry.register("form")(FormNode)
registry.register("decision")(DecisionNode)
registry.register("http")(HTTPNode)
registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)

# persist node with injected repository
repo = RedisRepository(redis_client)
registry.register("persist")(lambda: PersistNode(repo))

# custom node
@registry.register("send_email")
class SendEmailNode:
    async def run(self, context, params):
        ...

docs.title: Result & NodeError
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Result, NodeError

Every node returns either a Result (success path) or a NodeError (failure path). Both are immutable Pydantic models.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A successful node outcome.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description output dict[str, Any] {} Data merged into context.data by the runtime transition str "success" Key used to select the next state

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# default — success transition, no output
Result()

# with output data
Result(output={"user_id": 42, "created_at": "2025-01-15"})

# custom transition
Result(output={}, transition="needs_review")

# decision outcome
Result(transition="true")

docs.title: NodeError
docs.text: A failed node outcome.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description code str required Machine-readable error code message str required Human-readable description details dict[str, Any] {} Structured context — field errors, IDs, etc. transition str "failure" Key used to select the next state

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# validation error with per-field details
NodeError(
    code="VALIDATION_ERROR",
    message="Input validation failed",
    details={"age": "must be >= 0", "role": "must be one of ['admin', 'user']"},
)

# HTTP error
NodeError(
    code="HTTP_ERROR",
    message="HTTP 404",
    details={"status_code": 404, "url": "https://api.example.com/user/99"},
)

# custom transition routing
NodeError(
    code="PAYMENT_DECLINED",
    message="Card was declined",
    details={"reason": "insufficient_funds"},
    transition="declined",   # routes to "declined" state, not "failure"
)

docs.title: How the runtime uses them
docs.text:
result = await node.run(context, params)

# runtime reads the transition key from either type
next_node = node_def.transitions[result.transition]

# only Result carries output — NodeError output is ignored
if isinstance(result, Result):
    context = context.merge(result.output)

NodeError routes through the state machine exactly like Result. It does not terminate the workflow unless the "failure" transition leads to a terminal node.

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Runtime

Drives workflow execution. Resolves nodes, runs them, follows transitions, emits events, and returns the final context.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
Runtime(workflow: Workflow, registry: Registry)
Param Type Description workflow Workflow The state machine definition registry Registry Maps node type strings to node classes

docs.title: execute()
docs.text:
async def execute(
    execution_id: str,
    input_data: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    on_event: Callable | None = None,
) -> Context

Runs the workflow from start to completion.

Param Type Description execution_id str Unique identifier for this execution run input_data dict \| None Initial data placed in context.data on_event Callable \| None Called with each Event. Supports sync and async

Returns the final Context after the loop exits (context.node is None).

docs.title: Execution loop
docs.text:
Create Context(node=workflow.start, data=input_data)
↓
while context.node is not None:
    emit NODE_STARTED
    resolve and instantiate node from registry
    result = await node.run(context, params)
    emit NODE_COMPLETED
    validate transition exists
    emit TRANSITION_SELECTED
    context = merge output + advance node
↓
emit WORKFLOW_COMPLETED
return context

docs.title: Exception handling
docs.text:
If a node raises an unhandled exception, the runtime catches it and produces:

NodeError(code="UNEXPECTED_ERROR", message=str(exc))

The "failure" transition is then followed. If no "failure" transition exists on the node, the runtime raises RuntimeError.

docs.title: Unknown transitions
docs.text:
If a node returns a transition key not declared in the node's transitions dict, the runtime raises immediately:

RuntimeError: node 'verify_kyc': unknown transition 'approved'

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Runtime, Registry, Workflow, Node
from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode, ResponseNode

registry = Registry()
registry.register("form")(FormNode)
registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)

workflow = Workflow(
    id="w",
    start="collect",
    nodes={
        "collect": Node(
            type="form",
            params={"fields": {"name": {"type": "str"}}},
            transitions={"success": "done", "failure": "done"},
        ),
        "done": Node(type="response", transitions={"success": None}),
    },
)

runtime = Runtime(workflow, registry)

context = await runtime.execute(
    execution_id="exec_001",
    input_data={"input": {"name": "Alice"}},
    on_event=print,
)

print(context.data["response"])

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
from workflow_core import Workflow, Node

Defines the complete state machine. Immutable after construction.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id str Unique workflow identifier start str ID of the first node to execute nodes dict[str, Node] All states in the workflow

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Raises ValidationError at construction if: - start is not a key in nodes - Any transitions value (non-None) is not a key in nodes

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
workflow = Workflow(
    id="user_onboarding",
    start="collect_info",
    nodes={
        "collect_info": Node(
            type="form",
            params={"fields": {"name": {"type": "str"}}},
            transitions={"success": "respond", "failure": "respond"},
        ),
        "respond": Node(
            type="response",
            transitions={"success": None},
        ),
    },
)

docs.title: Node
docs.text: A single state in the workflow.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description type str required Maps to a registered node class in Registry params dict[str, Any] {} Static config passed to node.run() transitions dict[str, str \| None] {} Outcome key → next node id (or None to end)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Node(
    type="http",
    params={
        "method": "POST",
        "url": "https://api.example.com/verify",
        "body_key": "validated",
        "response_key": "verify_result",
    },
    transitions={
        "success": "next_step",
        "failure": "error_handler",
    },
)

docs.title: Terminal node
docs.text:
Node(type="response", transitions={"success": None})

A transition of None ends the workflow. The runtime exits the execution loop and returns the current context.

docs.title: DecisionNode
docs.text:
Evaluates a condition against context.data and routes to a branch.

from workflow_core.nodes import DecisionNode
registry.register("decision")(DecisionNode)

docs.title: Params
docs.text: Key Type Default Description key str required Key to read from context.data operator str "eq" Comparison operator value Any None Value to compare against

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: Operator Condition eq actual == value neq actual != value gt actual > value gte actual >= value lt actual < value lte actual <= value in actual in value not_in actual not in value exists actual is not None not_exists actual is None

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text: Key When "true" Condition matched "false" Condition did not match "failure" Invalid params (missing key, unknown operator)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# check string equality
Node(
    type="decision",
    params={"key": "kyc_status", "operator": "eq", "value": "approved"},
    transitions={"true": "create_account", "false": "reject"},
)

# check numeric threshold
Node(
    type="decision",
    params={"key": "score", "operator": "gte", "value": 700},
    transitions={"true": "approve_loan", "false": "manual_review"},
)

# check membership
Node(
    type="decision",
    params={"key": "role", "operator": "in", "value": ["admin", "superuser"]},
    transitions={"true": "admin_flow", "false": "user_flow"},
)

# check existence
Node(
    type="decision",
    params={"key": "existing_user", "operator": "exists"},
    transitions={"true": "conflict_response", "false": "create_user"},
)

docs.title: FormNode
docs.text:
Validates user-supplied input against a field schema.

from workflow_core.nodes import FormNode
registry.register("form")(FormNode)

docs.title: Params
docs.text: Key Type Default Description fields dict[str, FieldRules] {} Field definitions to validate source str "input" Key in context.data where input data lives

docs.title: FieldRules
docs.text: Key Type Description required bool Whether the field must be present. Default True type str "str", "int", "float", "bool" min int \| float Minimum value (int/float only) max int \| float Maximum value (int/float only) min_length int Minimum string length (str only) max_length int Maximum string length (str only) enum list Allowed values

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text: Key When "success" All fields pass validation "failure" One or more fields fail validation

docs.title: Output (on success)
docs.text:
Result(output={"validated": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "role": "admin"}})

Only fields defined in fields are included in validated.

docs.title: Output (on failure)
docs.text:
NodeError(
    code="VALIDATION_ERROR",
    message="Validation failed",
    details={"age": "must be >= 0", "role": "must be one of ['admin', 'user']"},
)

All failing fields are reported in a single NodeError.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Node(
    type="form",
    params={
        "source": "input",
        "fields": {
            "name": {"type": "str", "required": True, "max_length": 100},
            "age":  {"type": "int", "required": True, "min": 0, "max": 150},
            "role": {"type": "str", "required": True, "enum": ["admin", "user"]},
        },
    },
    transitions={"success": "next_step", "failure": "handle_error"},
)

docs.title: HTTPNode
docs.text:
Makes an async outbound HTTP request using httpx.

from workflow_core.nodes import HTTPNode
registry.register("http")(HTTPNode)

docs.title: Params
docs.text: Key Type Default Description url str required Request URL method str "GET" HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE body_key str \| None None context.data key to use as JSON request body response_key str "http_response" context.data key where response JSON is stored headers dict[str, str] {} Request headers

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text: Key When "success" HTTP 2xx response "failure" HTTP 4xx/5xx response, connection error, or missing url

docs.title: Output (on success)
docs.text:
Result(output={"http_response": { ...response JSON... }})

Use response_key to store under a different name:

params={"response_key": "kyc_result"}
# → Result(output={"kyc_result": {...}})

docs.title: Output (on failure)
docs.text:
# HTTP error
NodeError(code="HTTP_ERROR", message="HTTP 422", details={"status_code": 422, "url": "..."})

# Network error
NodeError(code="CONNECTION_ERROR", message="...", details={"url": "..."})

# Missing URL
NodeError(code="INVALID_PARAMS", message="'url' is required")

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# POST with body from context
Node(
    type="http",
    params={
        "method": "POST",
        "url": "https://kyc.example.com/verify",
        "body_key": "validated",
        "response_key": "kyc_result",
        "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer secret"},
    },
    transitions={"success": "check_kyc_status", "failure": "kyc_error"},
)

# GET request
Node(
    type="http",
    params={
        "method": "GET",
        "url": "https://api.example.com/user/profile",
        "response_key": "user_profile",
    },
    transitions={"success": "next", "failure": "error"},
)

docs.title: Note on HTTP clients
docs.text:
HTTPNode creates a new httpx.AsyncClient per execution. For high-throughput applications, register a factory that reuses a shared client:

shared_client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0)

class PooledHTTPNode(HTTPNode):
    def __init__(self, client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> None:
        self._client = client

    async def _request(self, method, url, json, headers):
        return await self._client.request(method=method, url=url, json=json, headers=headers)

registry.register("http")(lambda: PooledHTTPNode(shared_client))

docs.title: PersistNode
docs.text:
Reads from or writes to a storage backend via an injected Repository.

from workflow_core.nodes import PersistNode, Repository

PersistNode requires a Repository dependency. Register a factory:

repo = RedisRepository(redis_client)
registry.register("persist")(lambda: PersistNode(repo))

docs.title: Params
docs.text: Key Type Default Description key str required Storage key to read/write/delete operation str "write" "write", "read", or "delete" data_key str "validated" context.data key for the data to write (write only) output_key str "record" context.data key for the read result (read only)

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text: Key When "success" Operation succeeded "failure" Missing key param or unknown operation "failure" "read" — record not found (NOT_FOUND)

docs.title: write
docs.text:
Reads context.data[data_key] and stores it under key.

# writes context.data["validated"] to storage key "user:42"
params={"operation": "write", "key": "user:42", "data_key": "validated"}
# → Result(output={"persisted": True})

docs.title: read
docs.text:
Retrieves the record at key and stores it in context.data[output_key].

params={"operation": "read", "key": "user:42", "output_key": "user"}
# → Result(output={"user": {...record...}})
# or
# → NodeError(code="NOT_FOUND", message="Record 'user:42' not found")

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
Removes the record at key.

params={"operation": "delete", "key": "user:42"}
# → Result(output={"deleted": True})

docs.title: Repository protocol
docs.text:
from workflow_core.nodes import Repository

class Repository(Protocol):
    async def get(self, key: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None: ...
    async def set(self, key: str, value: dict[str, Any]) -> None: ...
    async def delete(self, key: str) -> None: ...

Implement this protocol to use any storage backend. The built-in Redis implementation ships in workflow_core.adapters.redis (see Adapters).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Node(
    type="persist",
    params={
        "operation": "write",
        "key": "user:new",
        "data_key": "validated",
    },
    transitions={"success": "respond_created", "failure": "persist_error"},
)

docs.title: ResponseNode
docs.text:
Shapes the final API response from context.data. Typically the terminal node in every workflow path.

from workflow_core.nodes import ResponseNode
registry.register("response")(ResponseNode)

docs.title: Params
docs.text: Key Type Default Description status int 200 HTTP status code include list[str] \| None None Keys to include from context.data. None includes everything

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Key When "success" Always

ResponseNode always succeeds. Use the workflow's terminal transition (None) after it.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Result(output={"response": {"data": {...}, "status": 200}})

The framework adapter reads context.data["response"] to build the HTTP response.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# success — include only specific fields
Node(
    type="response",
    params={"status": 201, "include": ["validated"]},
    transitions={"success": None},
)

# error — empty body
Node(
    type="response",
    params={"status": 409},
    transitions={"success": None},
)

# include everything in context
Node(
    type="response",
    params={"status": 200},
    transitions={"success": None},
)

docs.title: Reading the response
docs.text:
After execution:

context = await runtime.execute("exec_001", input_data={...})
response = context.data["response"]
# {"data": {...}, "status": 201}

docs.title: TransformNode
docs.text:
Maps and reshapes context.data fields using dot-path notation. Pure transformation — no I/O.

from workflow_core.nodes import TransformNode
registry.register("transform")(TransformNode)

docs.title: Params
docs.text: Key Type Description mapping dict[str, str] {target_key: source_path} — required, must be non-empty

docs.title: Dot-path notation
docs.text:
Source paths resolve nested keys using . as separator:

Path Resolves to "name" context.data["name"] "validated.name" context.data["validated"]["name"] "kyc_result.identity.score" context.data["kyc_result"]["identity"]["score"]

If a path does not resolve (key missing or intermediate is not a dict), that key is omitted from the output — no error.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text: Key When "success" Mapping applied (even if some paths were missing) "failure" mapping is empty or missing from params

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Result(output={"user_name": "Alice", "user_age": 30})

Only keys that resolved successfully are included.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# rename and flatten nested fields
Node(
    type="transform",
    params={
        "mapping": {
            "user_name":  "validated.name",
            "user_age":   "validated.age",
            "kyc_status": "kyc_result.status",
        }
    },
    transitions={"success": "persist_user", "failure": "error"},
)

# project top-level fields
Node(
    type="transform",
    params={
        "mapping": {
            "display_name": "name",
            "score":        "credit_score",
        }
    },
    transitions={"success": "respond"},
)

docs.title: UINode
docs.text:
Server-side rendering node with HTMX support. Combines form definition and template rendering into a single declaration. Handles GET (render) and POST (validate + transition) in one node.

from workflow_core.nodes import UINode
import jinja2

env = jinja2.Environment(loader=jinja2.FileSystemLoader("templates"))
registry.register("ui")(lambda: UINode(env))

docs.title: Params
docs.text:
Key Type Default Description template str required Template path relative to the Jinja2 environment loader partial_template str — Template used instead of template when request.is_htmx is True fields dict[str, FieldRules] {} Field definitions — same schema as FormNode source str "input" context.data key where POST input data lives

See FormNode for the full FieldRules schema.

docs.title: Request context
docs.text:
The node reads context.data["request"] to determine how to behave:

Key Type Description method str "GET" or "POST". Defaults to "GET" if absent is_htmx bool True if HX-Request header is present

The FastAPI adapter populates this before calling runtime.execute():

input_data={
    "request": {
        "method": request.method,
        "is_htmx": "HX-Request" in request.headers,
    },
    "input": await request.form(),
}

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text: Key When "render" GET — template rendered successfully "submitted" POST — all fields passed validation "error" POST — one or more fields failed validation; template re-rendered with errors "failure" Template not found or missing template param

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
Every template receives:

Variable Type Description data dict Full context.data — all accumulated execution state fields dict Field definitions from params.fields errors dict[str, str] Per-field error messages. Empty on GET execution_id str For use in form action URL node str Current node id

docs.title: Example template
docs.text:
{# templates/onboarding/_step1.html — HTMX partial #}
<form hx-post="/workflow/{{ execution_id }}/{{ node }}"
      hx-target="#content"
      hx-swap="innerHTML">

    {% for name, field in fields.items() %}
    <div class="field {% if errors.get(name) %}has-error{% endif %}">
        <label for="{{ name }}">{{ field.get('label', name) }}</label>
        <input
            id="{{ name }}"
            name="{{ name }}"
            type="{{ 'number' if field.type == 'int' else 'text' }}"
            value="{{ data.get(name, '') }}"
        />
        {% if errors.get(name) %}
        <p class="error">{{ errors[name] }}</p>
        {% endif %}
    </div>
    {% endfor %}

    <button type="submit">Continue</button>
</form>

docs.title: Workflow example — multi-step onboarding
docs.text:
Workflow(
    id="onboarding",
    start="step1",
    nodes={
        "step1": Node(
            type="ui",
            params={
                "template":         "onboarding/step1.html",
                "partial_template": "onboarding/_step1.html",
                "fields": {
                    "name":  {"type": "str", "required": True, "label": "Full Name"},
                    "email": {"type": "str", "required": True, "label": "Email"},
                },
            },
            transitions={
                "render":    None,
                "submitted": "step2",
                "error":     None,
            },
        ),
        "step2": Node(
            type="ui",
            params={
                "template":         "onboarding/step2.html",
                "partial_template": "onboarding/_step2.html",
                "fields": {
                    "age":  {"type": "int", "required": True, "min": 18, "label": "Age"},
                    "role": {"type": "str", "required": True,
                             "enum": ["admin", "user"], "label": "Role"},
                },
            },
            transitions={
                "render":    None,
                "submitted": "save",
                "error":     None,
            },
        ),
        "save": Node(
            type="persist",
            params={"operation": "write", "key": "user:new"},
            transitions={"success": "done", "failure": "done"},
        ),
        "done": Node(
            type="ui",
            params={"template": "onboarding/success.html"},
            transitions={"render": None},
        ),
    },
)

docs.title: HTMX routing in FastAPI
docs.text:
@router.api_route("/workflow/{execution_id}/{node_id}", methods=["GET", "POST"])
async def handle_ui_step(
    execution_id: str,
    node_id: str,
    request: Request,
):
    form_data = dict(await request.form()) if request.method == "POST" else {}

    context = await runtime.execute(
        execution_id=execution_id,
        input_data={
            "request": {
                "method": request.method,
                "is_htmx": "HX-Request" in request.headers,
            },
            "input": form_data,
        },
    )

    html = context.data.get("html", "")
    return HTMLResponse(content=html)
